newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds close stronger on positive U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds close stronger on positive U.S. data.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger on Tuesday with spreads to U.S. Treasuries widening as subdued U.S. economic data provided a boost to markets on both sides of the border, dealers said.

"Certainly the U.S. news was better than expected for the U.S. market. It (the Canadian market) has just been following suit," said Philip Strathy, chief investment officer with Strathy Investments Ltd. "The theory you can still have growth with no inflation bodes well for the bond market."
Canada's 30-year bond rose C$0.87 to C$108.35 to yield 7.282 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 32/32 to yield 6.77 percent. The spread between the bonds widened to 51 basis points from 49 basis points at the close of trading on Monday.

The U.S. Labor Department this morning reported U.S. consumer prices rose 0.3 percent, with the so-called core inflation rate up 0.1 percent. The U.S. Commerce Department also reported that December retail sales rose by 0.6 percent.

Both Canadian and U.S. bonds rallied following the data on short-covering gains, analysts said. Those gains were extended later in the morning and afternoon amid sudued Atlanta and Richmond Federal Reserve Bank and Johnson Redbook data.
Dealers said flows in the Canadian market were active initially following the data, but thinned out in the afternoon.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 rose C$0.62 to C$102.62 to yield 6.632 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 23/32 to yield 6.52 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds widened to 11 basis points from nine basis points at Monday's close.
The three-month cash bill traded with a yield of 2.88 percent against the U.S. bill which yielded 5.17 percent.
